items.name: Lon Men's Noodle House

gaps: Mediterranean and European section is underpowered on clearly food-specific, affordable-midrange candidates from allowed editorial domains; more Italian/Spanish/Greek/Balkan specialists should be sourced in a second pass if possible.

Several promising candidates lack exact street addresses in the search snippets (Hi! Chili, Chuan Garden, Mr. Noodle Chen, LIU Nudelhaus, Ma-Makan). These need the later Places step or an additional editorial-source pass for precise matching.
Vietnamese, Malaysian, Indonesian, Filipino, Lao, and Burmese representation is still thin relative to the Southeast Asian section brief; current set leans heavily Thai.
Turkish/Middle Eastern/Caucasus section is strong on Turkish specialists but weaker on Georgian, Armenian, Azerbaijani, Persian, and Yemeni candidates from allowed domains.
One fallback entry was forced into Mediterranean/European despite belonging more naturally to Southeast Asian; this section needs cleaner replacements before synthesis.
search_notes: Combined pass restricted to the user-approved domains only, with the strongest usable evidence coming primarily from Berlin Food Stories and Michelin Guide, plus one Berliner source. I excluded Chungking Noodles because a recent Berlin Food Stories news item says it closed at the end of April 2026. I did not use Google Maps or non-approved domains. Candidate quality is strongest for regional Chinese, Thai/Southeast Asian, Turkish specialists, and fine dining; weakest for Mediterranean/European and non-Thai Southeast Asian diversity. Several BFS snippets surfaced neighborhood and cuisine clearly but not always full street numbers, so those entries were retained only where the culinary case was strong enough to justify later Places verification.
